recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future work should target only a specific conformance statement if a reviewer identifies one that remains misleading after the existing introductory, parameter-support, and HTTP-method scoping text is considered.
issue_request: FHIR-36126 was Published/Persuasive for the FHIR-core search page. It asked that SHALL/SHOULD and similar search-page conformance requirements be qualified so they apply when an implementation supports search, not to every FHIR server regardless of capability.
initial_application: The issue was applied by a8509373541feb0c553e8c86dfe2bdf0136efee7, which made a first pass over source/search.html and changed the transport wording to “Servers supporting Search via HTTP”. Later e441170220c19e992f803667b245e63dcdd508cf moved the HTTP transport content to source/http.html while preserving the scoped wording.
additional_context: The originating Zulip thread shows the concern was whether the GET/POST SHALL from the search-method discussion applied only when search is supported. FHIR-I WGM minutes record a 10-0-0 persuasive vote. Current source/search.html says implementers need only implement needed search complexity and that servers are not required to implement standard search parameters; source/http.html scopes GET/POST requirements to servers supporting Search via HTTP/REST. Later FHIR-37753 conformance-statement tagging did not create a conflicting scoping decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scope source already conveys the intended conditional scope, and adding blanket repeated qualifiers to contextual search-processing statements would be redundant and potentially less clear.
